name: America Magazine
specific: You publish The Word on the Sunday readings every week, alongside daily Scripture reflections.
fit: Covers Catholic media, digital life and scripture resources for a readership heavy with teachers and catechists who recommend tools to others.
audienceDescription: Jesuit national review of faith and culture; educated lay Catholics, clergy, academics, educators
notes: Contact page also lists literaryeditor@americamagazine.org for book/literary reviews, ads@americamagazine.org for advertising and lmanico@americamagazine.org for press releases. The general editorial address is the honest route for a free-resource note; avoid the press-release address unless they ask.

name: Archdiocese of New York — Communications Office
specific: Your office runs The Good Newsroom and the archdiocese's monthly bulletin, which is what made me think of you.
fit: High reach, and the office maintains resource pages aimed at parishes and schools. Also the home of several Catholic media operations that take cues from archdiocesan channels.
audienceDescription: One of the largest and most visible archdioceses in the US, with a media office that fields national press and runs archdiocesan digital channels.
notes: Generic department address published in plain text; phone 646-794-2990. A large office, so expect a low reply rate — keep it to a few sentences.

name: Ascension (Ascension Presents, Fr. Mike Schmitz, Bible in a Year)
specific: The Bible in a Year sends a lot of people looking for somewhere to read along, and you already have your own app for that, so this is a note rather than a pitch.
fit: Their listeners are mid-habit on daily Scripture and constantly ask 'which Bible app should I use?'. A free offline one with no accounts answers that without pushing anyone toward a subscription.
audienceDescription: Huge mainstream Catholic audience, skewing younger; Bible in a Year made daily Scripture reading a mass-market habit for English-speaking Catholics.
notes: newsroom@ascensionpress.com is their published public-relations address — use that, not support@ or sales@. Be aware they sell their own Bible products and run a paid app, so a free app may read as competitive; pitch it as a resource for people who cannot pay, not as an alternative to them.

name: Busted Halo
specific: You keep a faith resources archive for ministry use, alongside the "In Two Minutes" explainers, which is what made me think of you.
fit: Aimed at young adults returning to or exploring the faith - exactly the group helped by a free Bible app with no account and no paywall.
audienceDescription: Paulist Fathers ministry for young adults and spiritual seekers; readers are 20s-40s Catholics and the loosely-affiliated
notes: Their 'Write for Us' page asks for a couple of paragraphs on what you want to write and why it fits; allow 2-3 weeks for a reply. They also list a separate advertise page, so keep the note clearly non-commercial.

name: Catholic Apostolate Center
specific: Your Catholic Media Links page, the one grouping Catholic news, television, magazines and blogs, is the sort of list I hoped this might belong on.
fit: They curate and republish free ministry resources for catechists, and they maintain the directory many parish accounts use to find each other — a listing there propagates.
audienceDescription: Catechists, parish and diocesan ministry leaders; they maintain widely used resource pages, including a curated list of Catholic Instagram accounts
notes: Their media page's email is obfuscated in the page source, so I did not record it; the page itself is the route. They also publish a phone number and mailing address.

name: Catholic Campus Ministry Association (CCMA)
specific: Your Recommended Reading page is the sort of list I hoped this might belong on.
fit: Campus ministers are the people who actually recommend Bible tools to students; CCMA's weekly newsletter is a clean, non-commercial way to reach them.
audienceDescription: Professional association of Catholic campus ministers; reaches ministers rather than students directly
notes: Contact page also lists stpierre@ccmanetwork.org (executive director) and an "Ask a Question" form. Start with the general admin address.

name: Catholic Education Resource Center (CERC)
specific: Your article library keeps standing Education and Faith and Character sections, which is the sort of place this might belong.
fit: A free-resource aggregator for Catholic educators — exactly the kind of site that lists genuinely free tools.
audienceDescription: Readers and educators across North America interested in Catholic education, faith and culture; large free article library
notes: Verified the address on their own contact page. Phone (703) 978-5753 published.

name: Catholic Icing
specific: You put out a new free printable Saint of the Day calendar each month, which is why I thought of writing.
fit: She already writes practical how-tos on using a Catholic study Bible with kids; a free offline Bible fits her "here's a thing that actually helps" format.
audienceDescription: Catholic moms, catechists and homeschool families (Lacy Lynch); long-running crafts and family-catechesis site
notes: Her contact page asks people to check the FAQ first and allows up to 72 hours for a reply — keep the note short and don't follow up quickly.

name: Catholic Productions (Dr. Brant Pitre)
specific: Mass Readings Explained goes through the Sunday readings week by week, which is what made me think of you.
fit: Weekly Gospel commentary listeners want the passage open while they listen; an offline Catholic Bible is a direct companion to what they already do every week.
audienceDescription: Scripture-serious lay Catholics and catechists following Dr. Pitre's Gospel-reading commentary and biblical studies lectures.
notes: Two named staff emails are published (Michael@ and Brian@CatholicProductions.com) plus phone (504) 305-1938. Small operation in Boutte, LA — a short personal note is more likely to be read here than a press release.

name: Catholic Review (Archdiocese of Baltimore)
specific: Rita Buettner's "Praying through the noise" ran in your commentary section this month, on finding prayer inside an ordinary busy day.
fit: Publishes practical items for local Catholics; a free, no-account Bible app is a low-friction recommendation for their parish readership.
audienceDescription: Newspaper of record for the Archdiocese of Baltimore; parishioners, parish and school communications staff
notes: They also run a dedicated 'Contact Us/News Tips' web form asking for a brief summary of the story idea - the form is arguably the better route than the general mailbox.

name: Catholic Schoolhouse
specific: Your three-year Tour cycle is built so everyone in a family studies the same memory work at a different level, which is what made me think of you.
fit: A chapter network means one conversation can reach many local Catholic homeschool co-ops with a free classroom-safe Scripture tool.
audienceDescription: Classical Catholic homeschool co-op network with local chapters across the US, grammar stage K-8
notes: They also publish kathy@catholicschoolhouse.com (Kathy Rabideau, co-founder) specifically for press/media requests — that is arguably the better address here, and it is published on the same page. Note the site's contact form uses a CAPTCHA; use the email instead of the form.

name: Catholic World Report
specific: Your Books section runs a steady stream of reviews of new Catholic titles, including Noelle Mering's No Contact this month.
fit: Serious Catholic readership that cares about translation and text fidelity; an offline Bible app is a natural short notice or review item.
audienceDescription: Ignatius Press global Church news and commentary; theologically engaged Catholic readers
notes: carl@ignatius.com is published on the About Us page as the editor's address (Carl E. Olson, Editor). Advertising goes to a different agency address (ads@carmelcommunications.com) - do not use it.

name: ChurchPOP
specific: Your recent piece on Cardinal Burke telling Gen Z not to let their phones imprison them made me hesitate before writing to you about anything that lives on a phone.
fit: Regularly runs listicles and round-ups of Catholic apps and free resources for a large, young lay audience - an ideal home for a 'free offline Catholic Bible app' mention.
audienceDescription: High-traffic Catholic pop-culture and viral-content site; young, social-media-native Catholic audience
notes: Their submissions page asks for 450-750 word pieces. The same address serves tips, so a short tip note is fine without writing the piece.

name: Crux
specific: Crux covers the Church as international news, with Vatican, Africa and Asia desks rather than resource round-ups, so I will keep this short.
fit: Explicitly invites 'publicists with Catholic developments' and story ideas at a dedicated tips address; covers Catholic digital life and resources.
audienceDescription: Independent international Catholic news site; readers are engaged Catholics, clergy, religious and Vatican-watchers
notes: Contact page distinguishes tips@cruxnow.com (editorial) from brennan@cruxnow.com (business/advertising) - use the tips address only, or it reads as an ad pitch.

name: Diocese of Buffalo — Communications Office
specific: Your office is the listed point of contact for the diocese's channels and the WNYCatholic feed, so this seemed the right door rather than emailing parishes one at a time.
fit: One named director, one published address, directly responsible for what the diocese shares with parishioners. A free no-ads Bible app is a low-friction thing for them to circulate.
audienceDescription: Western New York diocese; the communications director is the single published point of contact for the diocese's public channels.
notes: Gregory Tucker, Communication Director. The page literally says to contact him with questions, so unsolicited-but-relevant email is within the intended use of the address.

name: Diocese of Columbus — Office of Communications
specific: Your office puts out The Catholic Times several times a week with everything free to read online, no paywall, which is the reason I thought of sending this your way.
fit: A diocesan comms office is exactly the kind of place that maintains a 'free Catholic resources' list for parishes and catechists. A free, offline, no-accounts Bible app is easy for them to pass on to parish staff and RCIA leaders at no cost or risk.
audienceDescription: Roughly 275,000 Catholics across 23 central Ohio counties; the office runs the diocesan website, social channels and The Catholic Times, and distributes resources to parish bulletins and faith formation leaders.
notes: Full staff directory with individual emails is published in plain text (Jason Mays, Senior Director of Communications, jmays@columbuscatholic.org). The generic commailbox@ address is the more appropriate first approach. Ohio; English only.

name: Diocese of Harrisburg — Office of Public Relations / The Catholic Witness
specific: Between The Catholic Witness and the weekly Candid Catholic Convos radio program, your office puts a lot of resources in front of central Pennsylvania parishes.
fit: One of the better-staffed diocesan shops on this list, with a managing editor and a digital media specialist who both publish regularly. Genuine chance of a short write-up or a social mention of a free offline Bible app.
audienceDescription: Central Pennsylvania diocese with a seven-person communications team, a diocesan newspaper (The Catholic Witness), a multimedia producer and a digital media specialist.
notes: Rachel Bryson, Executive Director of Public Relations, 717-657-4804 x235. If the angle is editorial rather than institutional, Jennifer Reed, Managing Editor of The Catholic Witness, is jreed@hbgdiocese.org. All emails printed in plain text.

name: Diocese of Little Rock — Office of Catholic Campus Ministry
specific: You keep a public directory of Catholic campus ministry contacts at colleges across Arkansas, alongside the state's Mass, confession and adoration times.
fit: A single diocesan director who already curates and distributes resources to every campus ministry in the state — one email, many campuses. Students are the ideal audience for a free offline Bible app.
audienceDescription: Diocesan office coordinating Catholic campus ministry across Arkansas colleges and universities; maintains the public directory of campus ministry contacts statewide.
notes: Josh Salman, Diocesan Director of Campus Ministry, (501) 664-0340 ext. 333. Email printed in plain text. The diocese also publishes a statewide campus ministry locations page if per-campus follow-up is wanted.

name: Diocese of Saint Cloud — Communications / Media Relations
specific: Your office publishes The Central Minnesota Catholic and points readers to the daily Scripture readings from the diocesan resources page, which is the sort of place this might belong.
fit: They have an actual editorial staff writer and social media manager, meaning they publish resource round-ups rather than just press releases. A free offline Bible app fits their 'tools for your faith life' style of coverage.
audienceDescription: Central Minnesota diocese; the office publishes The Central Minnesota Catholic magazine and a diocesan news operation with a staff writer and social media manager.
notes: Kristi Anderson is Director of Communications, (320) 258-7650. Dianne Towalski is the social media manager (dianne.towalski@gw.stcdio.org) if the pitch is better aimed at a social post than an article.

name: Diocese of San Diego — Office of Communications
specific: The Southern Cross runs a genuine Spanish edition with its own reporting rather than a handful of translated pieces, which is rarer than it should be.
fit: Heavily bilingual, border-region diocese where an offline app that needs no account and no data connection genuinely matters for people with limited connectivity or prepaid phones.
audienceDescription: Large bilingual Southern California diocese; publishes The Southern Cross and runs substantial English and Spanish social channels.
notes: Aida Bustos, Director of Diocesan Media, (858) 490-8374. Leonardo Enrique Fonseca is Manager of Social Media (lfonseca@sdcatholic.org). Worth noting Spanish-language support (or its absence) explicitly in any approach here.

name: Diocese of Youngstown — Communications Department
specific: Your office produces Wineskins, the radio program and podcast of Scripture and saints reflections, which is what made me think of writing to you.
fit: Small enough office that a single person reads the inbox, and their remit is explicitly multimedia. Good odds of an actual human reply about a free resource for parishioners.
audienceDescription: Six-county northeastern Ohio diocese; the department handles media relations, multimedia and diocesan digital content.
notes: Dennis Biviano, Media Relations and Multimedia Specialist, 330-744-8451 x320. Email is printed in plain text on the page.

name: Dominican Friars, Province of St. Joseph
specific: Your student brothers publish to Dominicana every day, and Godsplaining comes out of the province as well.
fit: Probably the single best order-level fit here. Their whole public output is preaching and Scripture study for a young online audience, and 'editor@' is a published editorial address rather than a switchboard.
audienceDescription: The eastern US Dominican province — the friars behind Dominicana journal, the Godsplaining podcast and a large amount of online preaching and Scripture teaching. Audience skews young, online and Scripture-serious.
notes: Provincial office (212) 737-5757, 141 E 65th St, New York. A contact form with a topic dropdown is also on the same page. The Godsplaining podcast team is the informal route if the editorial one goes quiet.

name: Godsplaining (Dominican Friars, Province of St. Joseph)
specific: Recent episodes like "Do You Need Therapy, Prayer, or Both?" and "How to Discern What's Really Going On in Your Soul" are aimed at people actually trying to pray, which is what brought you to mind.
fit: Their listeners are young adults building prayer and reading habits on their phones; a free offline Bible fits the 'just start' advice the friars give constantly.
audienceDescription: Young adult Catholics; conversational theology, doubt, culture and practical faith from a team of Dominican friars. Strong podcast crossover.
notes: Email is published in the site footer. godsplaining.org/contact 404s — the footer address is the route. Friars rotate hosts, so address the show, not an individual.

name: Homeschool Connections
specific: Your recent post arguing that primary sources matter more than ever in the age of AI is roughly why I am writing.
fit: They maintain a public 'Catholic Homeschool Links' resources page and serve families who need Scripture tools for theology courses.
audienceDescription: Catholic homeschool families taking live and recorded online courses, grade school through high school, plus co-op partners
notes: They already curate a helpful-links page (homeschoolconnections.com/resources/helpful-links/) — that is the concrete ask.

name: Homiletic & Pastoral Review
specific: You publish a fresh set of homily helps every month, which is what made me think of you.
fit: Its clergy readership hands out resource recommendations parish-wide; a free offline Bible is useful for homily prep and for parishioners they advise.
audienceDescription: Journal for priests, deacons, seminarians and pastoral workers
notes: Book/resource reviews go to a separate published address: hprbooks@ignatius.com (Christopher Siuzdak, Book Reviews Editor). The reviews address is probably the better fit.

name: IgnatianSpirituality.com (Loyola Press, a Jesuit Ministry)
specific: Your Daily Examen page collects free guides, videos and a printable prayer card in one place, which is the kind of everyday prayer resource I had in mind.
fit: Ignatian prayer is Scripture-centred (imaginative contemplation of Gospel scenes), so a fast offline Gospel text is directly useful to their readers. The page explicitly invites ideas and submissions at this address.
audienceDescription: Jesuit-run spirituality site with the dotMagis blog, daily prayer resources and an email list; readers are prayer-practice oriented, including many parish and retreat leaders.
notes: The contact page states this address is for comments, ideas, questions and article submissions — so a resource suggestion is an in-scope use of it, not a cold sales pitch. Loyola Press, 8770 W. Bryn Mawr Ave., Suite 1125, Chicago. Do not use customerservice@loyolapress.com for this.

name: Life Teen
specific: Your blog tends to start from what teens are actually watching and work back to the faith, the way the "KPop Demon Hunters" pieces on spiritual warfare did.
fit: Youth ministers hand teens Scripture resources every week and need ones that are free and require no sign-up (a real issue with minors).
audienceDescription: Catholic high-school youth ministry network — youth ministers, core teams and teens across thousands of parishes
notes: Their contact page also publishes a full staff directory of individual addresses; use the general support address rather than picking a staff member's inbox out of the directory.

name: OSV Curriculum Division (Our Sunday Visitor)
specific: Your LifeLong Catechesis page posts the Sunday readings with backgrounds and lectionary correlations each week, free to anyone, which is what made me think of you.
fit: They publish free monthly downloadable activities for parents, teachers and catechists at TeachingCatholicKids.com — a natural place to mention a free Bible app.
audienceDescription: Catholic schools, parishes and dioceses using OSV catechetical curriculum; also runs the free TeachingCatholicKids.com resource site
notes: tscreligion@osv.com is published on the same page but is technical support for their platforms; customerservice@osv.com is the general published address. TeachingCatholicKids.com itself has no contact page (404) and no published email — go through OSV.

name: Petronille Press (Abigail Halpin)
specific: Most of your shop is printables a family can actually use at home — the St. Joseph paper altar, the O Antiphons banner, the saint coloring collections.
fit: Her audience is design-minded Catholics who care about how a devotional tool looks and feels, which is where a well-made free Bible app stands out.
audienceDescription: Professional illustrator and Catholic convert; religious prints and paper goods for Catholic families
notes: The address is published in the site header and footer (it is her design-studio domain, not the shop domain). There is no separate contact page — /pages/contact 404s.

name: Reason & Theology (Michael Lofton)
specific: Your course on the history of the biblical text, and segments like the one on the Muratorian Fragment, are what made me think of you.
fit: Debate-oriented viewers cross-reference Scripture constantly; a fast offline Catholic Bible with the deuterocanon is a practical tool for that audience.
audienceDescription: Mid-sized, highly engaged apologetics and ecclesiology audience; debates and long-form theological discussion, heavy Orthodox/Protestant crossover.
notes: Two published addresses (reasonandtheology@gmail.com and office@reasonmedia.org), a contact form and a phone number. Small independent operation — a direct personal note is appropriate.

name: Rose Harrington (Katrina Harrington)
specific: Your botanical Rosary art runs through all four sets of mysteries, and the Liturgy of the Flowers posts alongside it, which is what made me think of you.
fit: Her Scripture-lettering audience reads and shares individual verses constantly; a free verse-lookup Bible is directly useful to them.
audienceDescription: Catholic art buyers and prayer-focused followers; known for hand-lettered Scripture and botanical Rosary art
notes: Published email is a general shop inbox that also handles order questions — say up front that this is not an order issue.

name: Sensus Fidelium
specific: You post a Butler's Lives of the Saints entry most days alongside the longer sermons and the videos working through a Gospel parable with the Fathers.
fit: His audience values resources that are free of commercial entanglement and work without tracking or accounts — an offline, no-ads, no-login Bible app is an easy recommendation there.
audienceDescription: Large traditional-leaning Catholic audience; archive of sermons, talks and conferences used as a catechesis and doctrine library.
notes: Personal email plus a contact form and PO Box are published on the site. Traditional audience — emphasise the translation used and that nothing phones home. Do not overstate the subscriber figure; it came from a third-party stats site, not YouTube.

name: Seton Home Study School
specific: Seton Magazine, which you link from your site, runs Saint of the Month and Ask the Experts for the families you enroll.
fit: Their theology courses require daily Scripture reading; an offline Bible app with no account is useful for families with limited connectivity or device rules.
audienceDescription: One of the largest US Catholic home-study programs; thousands of enrolled homeschool families plus high-school theology and history departments
notes: Seton publishes a large set of departmental addresses. info@setonhome.org is the right general one; hstheology@setonhome.org is the high-school theology department if a more targeted note is wanted. Phone 540-636-9990.

name: Sophia Institute for Teachers
specific: Your online resource library and free eLessons are the sort of list I hoped this might belong on.
fit: Their whole model is giving Catholic teachers free/low-cost classroom-ready faith resources. A free, offline, no-account Bible app is something a teacher can point a whole class or a parish program to without licensing or logins.
audienceDescription: Catholic K-12 school teachers, parish catechists and diocesan faith formation offices; the site states a community of roughly 60,000 educators
notes: Largest and best-matched single contact in this segment. General customer service inbox, so the note should be short and clearly aimed at their editorial/resources team. Per the requester: do not name the developer, present it only as a free app found on the App Store.

name: St. Paul Center for Biblical Theology (Scott Hahn, John Bergsma)
specific: Your Word of the Lord reflections walk through the Sunday Mass readings each week with Dr. Hahn and Dr. Bergsma, which is what made me think of you.
fit: The single closest audience match in this segment: their viewers are, by definition, people who want to read the Bible as Catholics. Offline access matters for study groups meeting in parish halls with bad signal.
audienceDescription: Catholic Bible study audience — parish study groups, catechists and adults working through Scripture in the Catholic tradition.
notes: Email, contact form, phone (740-264-9535) and a separate speaker-inquiry form all published. Based in Steubenville, OH.

name: The Catholic Art Company
specific: You arrange the shop by collection — Christ the King, Mary Mother of God, Saints and Blesseds — with the stated aim of bringing two thousand years of Catholic art into ordinary homes.
fit: Their stated mission is enriching Catholic homes with the truths of the faith; pairing sacred art posts with a free Scripture app is a natural fit.
audienceDescription: Catholic families buying classic sacred art prints; also on Facebook and X (@catholicartco)
notes: The published address is a named personal inbox on the company domain, printed on their own contact page alongside a phone number.

name: The Catholic Gentleman (Sam Guzman)
specific: Your videos this past month have been mostly on marriage and fatherhood, including the one on what a daughter needs from her father.
fit: Daily Scripture reading is a standing theme for their audience, and 'no ads, no account, works offline' fits the digital-minimalism thread that runs through their content.
audienceDescription: Mid-sized audience of Catholic men on formation, prayer discipline and practical spirituality; podcast plus written content.
notes: Email published alongside a form with a purpose dropdown that includes 'podcast ideas' — that is the right category to use.

name: The Catholic Spirit (Archdiocese of Saint Paul and Minneapolis)
specific: Your Focus on Faith section runs a Sunday Scriptures column and sends readers to the day's readings, which is what made me think of you.
fit: Diocesan papers run short 'useful resources' and Lent/Advent round-ups; a free Bible app fits that slot and reaches catechists and parish staff directly.
audienceDescription: Official archdiocesan newspaper; parishioners, parish staff and Catholic school families across the Twin Cities
notes: Contact page also publishes ruffj@archspm.org (Joe Ruff, publications manager, news/editorial) and a news tips hotline at (651) 251-7702. Seasonal timing (Advent, Lent) matters for diocesan papers.

name: The Tablet
specific: Your Living Spirit feature runs each week with the coming liturgical calendar and a few short meditations set beside it.
fit: Reaches a large UK and international Catholic readership including parish and school staff who pass resource tips along.
audienceDescription: Long-running UK international Catholic weekly; clergy, religious, educators and lay readers in Britain and worldwide
notes: Contact page also publishes letters@thetablet.co.uk for letters and mfergusson@thetablet.co.uk for the Deputy/Literary Editor. Note the app is NRSV-based, which lands well with this readership.

name: Thomistic Institute (Aquinas 101)
specific: Aquinas 101 and your recommended reading lists already put a lot of free, structured material in students' hands.
fit: Their learners are already doing homework-style study and need the text at hand; an offline Bible app with no account friction suits students on campus wifi or on the move.
audienceDescription: University students, serious lay learners and educators working through Catholic philosophy and theology; Aquinas 101 is widely used as a structured course.
notes: Email, phone ((202) 495-3843) and a contact form are all published on their contact page. Run by the Dominican House of Studies in Washington DC — an academic tone lands better than a marketing one.

name: U.S. Catholic
specific: You publish a Sunday reflection on the week's Mass readings every week, most recently Daniel Horan's for September 20.
fit: Publishes short reviews of Catholic books, media and resources for a lay readership; a genuinely free, no-ads, no-account offline Bible is the kind of practical resource their reviews section covers.
audienceDescription: National Catholic magazine (Claretian Missionaries) read by lay Catholics, parish staff, catechists and social-justice-minded readers; runs a regular reviews section
notes: editors@uscatholic.org is stated on the contact page as the route for 'General queries and press releases'. They also publish a separate reviews route: https://uscatholic.org/submit-a-review/ (reviews capped around 400 words). Do not pitch this as advertising - they have a separate advertising@uscatholic.org address and will bounce promo there.

name: USCCB — Office of Public Affairs
specific: Your office is the one that puts out the backgrounders and the "How to Cover the Catholic Mass" guide, so plain reference material seems to sit in your lane.
fit: The USCCB publishes the NABRE text and maintains the most-used Catholic Bible resources online. If a free offline Catholic Bible app is on their radar, diocesan offices follow. Realistically a long shot, but the address is explicitly published for media inquiries.
audienceDescription: National bishops' conference press office; the reference point for US Catholic media and for every diocesan communications office in the country.
notes: Page states media inquiries are welcomed at this address, 202.541.3200. Do not expect a promotional response — treat it as informational. Note that the USCCB is protective of NABRE licensing, so any approach should be clear about which translation the app uses and under what permission.

name: Word on Fire
specific: You publish a Gospel reflection for every single day, which is what made me think of you.
fit: They point followers to free Scripture and study resources constantly, and their audience skews toward people who read daily.
audienceDescription: Very large evangelisation audience around Bishop Barron; heavy Scripture and catechesis content
notes: The media address appeared in the indexed text of their own contact page, but wordonfire.org returns 403 to automated fetches, so I could not load the page myself — open it in a browser and confirm before sending. They also publish contact@wordonfire.org for general/partnership requests.

name: Word on Fire (Bishop Robert Barron)
specific: Your article this week on the new Bible study opportunity for evangelists is what prompted me to write.
fit: Enormous reach and a Scripture-first output. Realistically the least likely to respond, but they maintain a genuine press kit and communications address, and the cost of one short email is nothing.
audienceDescription: The largest Catholic digital evangelization ministry in the English-speaking world — millions of YouTube subscribers, a major podcast, daily Gospel reflections by email.
notes: They publish a press kit page with a communications contact and an interview request form. I could not fetch the page directly (the site blocks automated fetches), so I am not reporting an email I did not read myself — open the press kit page to get the current address. Expect no reply; do not follow up more than once.

name: Ascension (Ascension Presents / Fr. Mike Schmitz)
fit: Their entire audience is mid-way through a daily Scripture plan and constantly asks 'which Bible app should I use offline?'. A free, no-ads, no-account Catholic Bible is a natural companion resource for Bible-in-a-Year listeners.
audienceDescription: Mainstream US Catholics who follow Fr. Mike Schmitz; the same org produces 'The Bible in a Year' and 'The Rosary in a Year' podcasts, which are the single biggest on-ramp to daily Scripture reading in the English-speaking Catholic world.
notes: Their contact page lists a dedicated Public Relations address (newsroom@ascensionpress.com) separate from support@ and sales@ — use the newsroom one. They are a publisher with commercial Bible products, so frame this purely as a free resource, not a partnership or promotion.

name: Bible Study Evangelista (Sonja Corbitt)
audienceSize: Not publicly stated in a form I could verify
fit: Her entire method is a modernised lectio divina built on working directly with the biblical text — a free offline Bible removes the main practical barrier for participants who do not own a study Bible.
audienceDescription: Catholic women doing structured Bible study; Sonja Corbitt teaches the LOVE the Word lectio divina method and hosts the Evangelista Bible Study show on CatholicTV.
notes: She publishes the address spaced out ('hello.sonjacorbitt @ gmail.com') as light scrape protection, so write it out normally but do not bulk-mail it. Phone 615.669.2491 is also published. Her speaking calendar is reportedly booked well ahead — keep it to a short resource note, not a request for her time.

name: Breaking in the Habit (Fr. Casey Cole, OFM)
fit: His audience is heavily 'new to this' Catholics and returners — exactly the people who want a Bible app but balk at sign-ups, ads or in-app purchases.
audienceDescription: Mid-to-large audience of young adult Catholics, seekers and the curious; friendly explainer-style catechesis from a Franciscan friar.
notes: This is an explicitly published media-inquiry address on his own press kit page, which is the cleanest possible route. Franciscan — the no-cost, no-ads angle will land well with him.

name: Catechist's Journey (Loyola Press)
fit: A Jesuit-run blog whose readers are catechists hunting for practical, free tools for sessions and for families to use at home.
audienceDescription: Catechists, parish faith-formation leaders and religious educators across age groups
notes: The only email published on the contact page is the Loyola Press general customer service address, so the note may need forwarding internally to the blog editors. Phone 800-621-1008 also published.

name: Catholic Central (Family Theater Productions, Holy Cross)
fit: Their content lands in classrooms and youth groups, where a free app with no accounts and no ads is often the only thing that clears a school's approval bar.
audienceDescription: Explainer-style catechesis for teens, young adults and classrooms; widely used by Catholic school teachers and youth ministers.
notes: Published newsroom/PR address (Chris Sariego) for Family Theater Productions, which produces Catholic Central. catholiccentral.com itself publishes no contact details, so the parent org's newsroom is the correct route.

name: Companions of the Cross (Fr. Mark Goring)
fit: His viewers watch short daily videos and are prompted constantly to go read the passage themselves; an offline Bible app is the obvious next tap.
audienceDescription: Large daily-devotional audience; short videos on prayer, Scripture and spiritual life from a priest of the Companions of the Cross.
notes: info@companionscross.org is the community's general address, not Fr. Goring's personal one — it will be triaged by the order, so say clearly it is for him. Phone 613-728-3175 (Ottawa) / 1-866-885-8824 also published.

name: Daily Rosary Meditations (Holy Family School of Faith)
audienceSize: 22.9K YouTube subscribers (their daily Rosary podcast audience is far larger)
fit: Their whole model is daily habit formation around Scripture-based Rosary meditation, and they run mentorship groups who would benefit from a free Bible they can hand to every participant at zero cost.
audienceDescription: Daily Rosary meditation listeners led by Dr. Mike Scherschligt; strongly formation-minded, many in parish small groups and mentorship programs.
notes: dailyrosary.net is the show's site but publishes no contact details; the address is in the site-wide footer of the parent organisation, schooloffaith.com. An established non-profit — expect a slower, more formal reply.

name: Holy Rosary Today
fit: Their viewers already use their phone as a prayer tool daily. An offline Bible with no ads and no account fits the same 'just open it and pray' habit, and their Scripture-based Rosary meditations pair directly with it.
audienceDescription: Daily Rosary pray-along audience — largely older Catholics and families who pray with the video each evening.
notes: Email is printed on the site itself; there is also a contact form reachable from the 'Support Us' footer link. A small independent apostolate — keep the note short and personal.

name: Salt + Light Media
audienceSize: Not publicly stated in a form I could verify
fit: They broadcast prayer and Adoration to a bilingual audience that often watches on mobile, and they maintain lists of free Catholic resources for viewers.
audienceDescription: Canadian Catholic media network — daily Mass, Rosary, Adoration broadcasts and Scripture reflections, in English and French, with a US arm as well.
notes: info@saltandlighttvusa.org is published for the US entity. Offices in Toronto (416.971.5353), Montreal and Washington DC. If the app has a French option, lead with that — it is a genuine differentiator for them.

name: Shalom World / Shalom Media
audienceSize: Not publicly stated in a form I could verify
fit: Their Adoration livestream viewers pray with a device already in hand, and their international audience often has patchy connectivity — offline access is a genuine, not cosmetic, benefit.
audienceDescription: Global Catholic TV network with 24/7 Eucharistic Adoration livestreams from their Prayer Chapel, plus Rosary, Scripture and devotional programming. Strong reach in the US, India, UK, Australia and Ireland.
notes: Regional addresses are also published (canada@, uk@, australia@, ireland@, austria@shalomworld.org) if a country-specific angle is useful. Large organisation — the general info@ address may take a while to route.

name: The Catholic Woman
fit: Reader-submitted, resource-friendly format; their audience is young adults who read Scripture on their phones rather than carrying a Bible.
audienceDescription: Catholic women, mostly young adult, reading weekly letters from other women about faith and vocation
notes: Site is on the .co domain but the published address uses .com — use it exactly as published, and the contact form is a safe fallback.

name: The Thomistic Institute
audienceSize: Not publicly stated in a form I could verify
fit: Their campus chapters run Scripture and contemplative-prayer groups where students need a free Bible on hand; cost is a real barrier for that audience.
audienceDescription: University students and intellectually serious Catholics; Dominican-run lectures on Scripture, prayer, contemplation and Aquinas, with a large campus-chapter network.
notes: Run by the Dominican House of Studies. Also published: (202) 495-3843 and 487 Michigan Ave NE, Washington, DC 20017.

name: USCCB — Daily Reflections video series
fit: They are the reference point for US parish and diocesan communications staff. Even a listing or a pass-along reaches catechists nationwide, and their Daily Reflections audience is precisely people reading Scripture every day.
audienceDescription: The US bishops' own daily Mass-readings and video reflection audience, plus the diocesan and parish communications staff who redistribute it.
notes: This is an institutional media-relations desk, not a creator — expect a formal, slow, possibly no response. Realistically the better use is as background; the diocesan-communications segment is a warmer route. Phone 202.541.3200.

name: Aleteia (English edition)
fit: Huge general Catholic audience and frequent 'best Catholic apps' and prayer-resource round-ups; multilingual reach is a bonus.
audienceDescription: Very large international Catholic lifestyle and spirituality site published in multiple languages
language: English (also FR, ES, IT, PT, PL, AR)
notes: Their contact page publishes a dedicated editorial address for the English edition, but the page obfuscates addresses so I could not read it verbatim. An address of the form editorial_en@aleteia.org appears in search indexes of that page - verify it in a browser before using. Their advertising contact is separate; do not use it, since this is not an ad.

name: Archdiocese of Washington — Office of Communications
fit: Well-resourced office serving a large, diverse, highly online Catholic population, including many university students.
audienceDescription: Archdiocese covering DC and five Maryland counties; the communications office handles media questions and archdiocesan content.
notes: The page publishes an Office of Communications email and the phone 301-853-4516, but the address is rendered behind anti-scraping protection so I did not read it directly — open the page rather than assuming the pattern. Phone is confirmed.

name: Arlington Catholic Herald
fit: Serves one of the most active US dioceses with a large Catholic school and catechetical network that shares resource recommendations.
audienceDescription: Diocese of Arlington (Northern Virginia) newspaper; parishioners, Catholic school families, parish staff
notes: Staff emails on the contact page are hidden behind Cloudflare email protection, so no address is recorded. Use the 'Submit a story idea' link on that page. Executive Editor is Kevin Schweers; Managing Editor is Ann M. Augherton. Phone 703-841-2590.

name: Association for Catechumenal Ministry (ACM)
fit: OCIA catechumens are usually new to Scripture and often need a Bible immediately and for free — the single best-matched RCIA-specific contact in this segment.
audienceDescription: Parish and diocesan OCIA/RCIA directors, catechumenate team members and catechists across the US
notes: Email on the homepage is Cloudflare-protected, so not reported. Contact page and phone 513-543-5477 are the published routes.

name: Augustine Institute
fit: They sit upstream of thousands of parish catechists. If it ends up on a parish resource list, reach compounds well beyond the channel's own subscriber count.
audienceDescription: Catechetical publisher and graduate school behind FORMED; audience is parishes, DREs, Catholic school staff and adult formation leaders.
notes: Their contact page publishes a form, a phone number ((314) 557-0847) and inquiry categories including 'parish and school resources' and 'media and publishing' — that is the right category. Search results mention info@augustineinstitute.org but I did not see it on the page itself, so I am not recording it. They also sell catechetical products, so lead with the parish-resource angle.

name: BARITUS Catholic Illustration (Chris Lewis)
fit: He already works with parishes and schools on sacramental-event materials, so he has a direct line to parish audiences who could use a free Bible app.
audienceDescription: Catholic illustration audience, plus parishes and schools that order custom holy cards, tees and stickers
notes: Form only; the /pages/contact and /pages/contact-us paths 404 — the working URL is /contact.

name: Bible Christian Society (John Martignoni)
fit: His entire apostolate is built on giving Catholic apologetics material away free, and his content is wall-to-wall Scripture citation. Philosophically the closest match in the segment.
audienceDescription: Long-running free Catholic apologetics audience — mailing list, free downloadable talks, heavily Scripture-verse driven.
notes: Form only. His contact page states he is not taking further apologetics questions due to volume, but explicitly still welcomes feedback, suggestions and other contact — frame the note as a resource suggestion, not a question.

name: Blessed Is She
fit: Their entire daily rhythm is built on reading the day's Scripture; an offline Bible app is a natural companion for readers who are away from their printed devotional.
audienceDescription: Large community of Catholic women using daily Scripture devotionals; they publish their own Catholic notetaking/journaling Bible
notes: Only a contact page/form is published; I did not find an official partnership email on their own site. Ignore third-party "email format" databases — those are guessed patterns, not published addresses.

name: Brian Holdsworth
fit: He is a designer by trade and frequently critiques the attention economy; an ad-free, account-free, offline app is exactly the kind of thing he engages with on its own merits.
audienceDescription: Mid-sized (roughly 100k-200k) audience for essay-style videos on Catholic faith, tradition, liturgy and modern culture. Canadian.
notes: Form only — no email published. He is a one-man operation, so keep it short and concrete; he will judge the app on craft.

name: Busted Halo (Paulist Fathers)
fit: Their audience is exactly the person who downloads a Bible app and wants no account and no subscription. They already publish app and resource round-ups for young adults.
audienceDescription: Paulist-run online magazine, video channel and SiriusXM show aimed at young adult and 'returning' Catholics; weekly newsletter, large YouTube presence for explainer videos.
notes: The contact form has an explicit 'Press/Media Inquiries, Speaking Engagements' option in its reason dropdown — use that option, it is the intended route. The only plain-text email on the page, BustedHalo@TheCatholicChannel.org, is specifically for the SiriusXM radio show producer, so do not use it for a general pitch. 405 W. 59th Street, New York.

name: CATECHIST Magazine (Pflaum)
fit: A long-standing trade publication for catechists; free classroom/parish tools are core to what they cover.
audienceDescription: Parish catechists, DREs and Catholic school religion teachers in the US
notes: The page does publish an email but it is deliberately obfuscated by an anti-spam plugin (shown as se*****@ba*******.com), so I am not reporting a guessed address. Use the on-page form. Phone listed publicly as (800) 558-2292. Page also states they are no longer accepting article submissions.

name: Capturing Christianity (Cameron Bertuzzi)
fit: His crossover viewers are exactly the people who need a Catholic Bible including the deuterocanonical books, often for the first time, and would rather not pay to find out.
audienceDescription: Philosophy-of-religion and apologetics audience, Christian and non-Christian; the host entered the Catholic Church and now draws a strong Catholic-curious Protestant crossover.
notes: Form only — no email published. Broadly Christian rather than exclusively Catholic, so pitch the app as the Catholic canon reference his audience keeps asking about.

name: Catholic Answers
fit: Apologetics followers need fast verse lookup; a free offline Catholic Bible with the deuterocanon is directly useful to them.
audienceDescription: Large apologetics audience that argues from Scripture constantly; roughly 392k on Instagram per public profile listings
notes: No published press email — the general contact form with a department selector is the honest route.

name: Catholic Answers (incl. The Counsel of Trent / Trent Horn, Jimmy Akin)
fit: Apologetics audiences are constantly asked to 'look up the verse.' A free offline Catholic Bible with no ads and no sign-in is the cleanest possible thing to recommend to someone mid-argument or mid-RCIA.
audienceDescription: Apologetics-first audience: Catholics defending the faith, converts, and Protestant/atheist interlocutors. Trent Horn's Counsel of Trent and Jimmy Akin's channel sit under the same staff roof.
notes: No public email published — form only, with a department dropdown (Customer Service, Webmaster, Publishing, Radio, Advertising, Parish Ministry). No press/media option, so 'Customer Service' or 'Webmaster' is the realistic route. Trent Horn's trenthornpodcast.com/contact redirects to Patreon, so go through catholic.com rather than chasing him directly.

name: Catholic Apptitude
fit: Maintains a large curated directory of Catholic apps and an explicit 'Your Recommendations' page inviting app suggestions - a direct, invited listing route.
audienceDescription: Directory and review site for Catholic apps, produced as a digital-ministry project associated with Xt3 (Catholic Archdiocese of Sydney)
notes: No email published; contact form only (Name, Email, Website, Comment). They also have a dedicated submission page at catholicapptitude.org/your-recommendations/ which is the more appropriate route. Much of the site's dated content is old, so confirm it is still maintained.

name: Catholic Heritage Curricula (CHC)
fit: They already run a 'free resources as part of our mission' page, so a genuinely free Catholic Bible app is on-mission for that page rather than an ad.
audienceDescription: Catholic homeschooling families using CHC curriculum; they maintain a public free-resources library
notes: No email published on the free-resources page; the site's contact form is the route. Their free-resources page is the natural place for a link, so frame the note around that page specifically.

name: Catholic Paper Goods (Shari Van Vranken)
fit: Her printables are used in parish religious-education classrooms, so she reaches catechists who hand out Scripture resources weekly.
audienceDescription: Catechists, homeschoolers and parish volunteers using her printable saints coloring pages and cards
notes: Her site presented an SSL chain error to my fetcher, so I could not load the contact page myself; the contact-us URL is indexed and a shari@catholicpapergoods.com address appears in search summaries, but I did not see it on the page — verify in a browser before using it, otherwise use the form.

name: Catholic Sprouts
fit: Parents want a Bible their kids can open without an account, ads, or an in-app store — that is the single strongest selling point of this app for this audience.
audienceDescription: Catholic parents and homeschoolers (Nancy Bandzuch); daily kids' podcast plus family faith-formation products
notes: Form only on the shop site. A weekly Sunday-evening family-resources newsletter is where a mention would most plausibly land.

name: Catholic-Link
audienceSize: ~548k on the Spanish account per third-party analytics (not an official figure)
fit: Their whole output is shareable Scripture and catechesis graphics; a free, no-ads, offline Catholic Bible is exactly the kind of resource they round up for readers, and the Spanish side reaches an audience that is often underserved by free Catholic apps.
audienceDescription: Broad Catholic audience for infographics, Scripture graphics, memes and catechetical explainers; heavily shared by catechists and youth ministers
notes: Contact page has a form only (with a simple math anti-spam field) — no published email. Two language editions, so say which audience the note is for.

name: CatholicApps.com
fit: The single most on-target outlet in this segment - it exists specifically to review Catholic apps, and its readers arrive already searching for one.
audienceDescription: Niche review site for Catholic iOS and Android apps; readers are Catholics actively looking for apps
notes: No email is published; the contact page is a plain form (Name, email, Comment or Message). Worth checking whether the site is still actively updated before investing effort.

name: CatholicTV Network
fit: Their daily Rosary and Bible study viewers skew toward people who want a simple, free, no-subscription tool, and the network regularly points viewers to free Catholic resources.
audienceDescription: US Catholic television network; broadcasts the Rosary daily, plus Bible study programming including the Evangelista Bible Study show.
notes: Form only; no email published. Also published: P.O. Box 9196, Watertown, MA 02471 and 617-923-0220.

name: Detroit Catholic (Archdiocese of Detroit)
fit: Active diocesan newsroom covering Catholic life and resources for a large metro Catholic population.
audienceDescription: Archdiocese of Detroit news outlet; local Catholics, parish and school staff
notes: No public editorial email is published - the page says to use the form for 'news tips, story ideas or other questions'. They state they read every submission but cannot reply to each pitch. News operations phone is (313) 596-7109.

name: Diocese of Cleveland — Communications Department
fit: Big diocese with a real communications operation and a long history of publishing parish resource lists.
audienceDescription: Large northeast Ohio diocese; the communications department handles all diocesan media and public content.
notes: Honest answer: no email address of any kind is published on this page — only phone numbers, (216) 696-6525 and (800) 869-6525, and a mailing address. Phone or post is the only public route I could verify. Lower priority than the dioceses above for that reason.

name: Diocese of Dallas — Media Inquiries
fit: Very large, very bilingual diocese. Free and offline matters more in communities where data plans are tight, and the diocese has the reach to make a mention count.
audienceDescription: One of the largest and fastest-growing US dioceses, heavily Hispanic, with a dedicated public media inquiries channel.
notes: No named contact or email is published; the diocese deliberately routes everything through the form on this page. Phone (214) 528-2240. Keep the form submission short — it has a plain message box.

name: Diocese of Fort Wayne–South Bend — Secretariat for Communications
fit: Editorial plus social content roles in one office, and a young campus-heavy population nearby. An offline Bible app travels well among students.
audienceDescription: Indiana diocese; five-person secretariat including an editorial program manager and a social media content creator. Home diocese of Notre Dame, so unusually connected to Catholic higher-ed audiences.
notes: Emily Mentock is Secretary for Communications, Scott Warden is Editorial Program Manager. Office line (260) 271-7295. The office email is published on the page but encrypted against scrapers; a person can read it.

name: Diocese of Joliet, Department of Catechesis and Evangelization
fit: Diocesan catechesis offices pass resources down to every parish program at once; a good template for the wider diocesan approach.
audienceDescription: Parish catechetical leaders and catechists across the Diocese of Joliet, Illinois
notes: The page lists named staff with direct emails and phone numbers, but the addresses were masked in what I could retrieve, so I have not reported them. Craig Mazur (Interim Director, 815-221-6134) and Dcn. Anthony Clishem (Catechetical Formation, 815-221-6142) are the relevant names; read the emails off the live page. Same pattern works for other diocesan catechesis offices (Archdiocese of Washington, Archdiocese of Indianapolis, Diocese of Austin, Diocese of Lincoln) if you want to scale this.

name: Diocese of Orange — Office of Communications
fit: The only diocese I found with a named 'Youth & Young Adult Digital Media Strategist' — a role whose whole job is finding digital tools worth putting in front of young Catholics. Strong fit for an app.
audienceDescription: Large Orange County, California diocese with a ten-person communications team covering OC Catholic newspaper, OC Catholic Radio, social media and a dedicated youth/young adult digital media strategist.
notes: Noah Fonacier holds the youth/young adult digital media role and is the sharpest target here; Jarryd Gonzales is Head of Communications, desk 714-282-3075. All addresses on the page are obfuscated against scrapers but visible to a human visitor — open the page rather than guessing the pattern.

name: Diocese of Wichita — Office of Communications / The Catholic Advance
fit: They run a print newspaper plus diocesan digital channels, so they regularly cover resources parishioners can actually use.
audienceDescription: Kansas diocese with a four-person communications team and a diocesan newspaper, The Catholic Advance.
notes: Marie Fiebach is Director of Communications (316-440-1746) and Del Torkelson edits The Catholic Advance. Their email addresses ARE published on the page but are rendered behind anti-scraping obfuscation, so I could not read them without bypassing that — a human opening the page will see them plainly. Use the page, not a guessed address.

name: Discerning Hearts
fit: They publish a daily lectio divina series — the practice depends on having the text of Scripture immediately to hand. A free offline Bible is the most directly useful tool their listeners could be given.
audienceDescription: Contemplative and spiritual-formation audience: daily lectio divina, Carmelite and Ignatian spirituality, spiritual direction series with priests and religious.
notes: No public email; they route everything through a form (the form itself is hosted at donate.discerninghearts.net/contact-us/). They also run their own app, so present this as a complementary free resource, not a competitor.

name: Down to Earth Ministry (Keith Nester)
fit: His viewers arrive already reading Scripture daily and need a Catholic edition; 'free, offline, nothing to sign up for' removes the last obstacle for someone still just exploring.
audienceDescription: Former Protestant pastor now Catholic; audience is converts, seekers and Protestants looking honestly at Catholicism. Very Bible-literate.
notes: Note the domain change: downtoearthministry.org redirects to down2earthministry.org. Form only, plus phone 717-367-0100 and an address in Elizabethtown, PA. Operates under Stewardship: A Mission of Faith.

name: Dr. Taylor Marshall
fit: Large audience that values Catholic resources independent of big platforms and commercial tracking.
audienceDescription: Large traditional-leaning Catholic commentary and catechesis audience.
notes: No contact page, no published email, no press page on taylormarshall.com — only newsletter signup, a support page and a store. I am listing him as none-found rather than guessing an address. He is also a polarising figure within the Church; worth deciding deliberately whether you want the app associated with that channel before spending effort finding a route.

name: EWTN News / Catholic News Agency
fit: Wire pickup means a single short item can reach dozens of diocesan papers and their catechist readers.
audienceDescription: Major international Catholic wire service; its stories are picked up by diocesan papers worldwide
notes: CNA's contact page now redirects to EWTN News (CNA and ACI Prensa were folded into EWTN News in January 2026). The live page offers only a contact form - no email addresses are published on it. Several addresses circulate in search indexes; I could not verify any on the page, so none is recorded.

name: Every Sacred Sunday
fit: Their product is built entirely around the Sunday readings; followers already look for ways to sit with Scripture during the week.
audienceDescription: Young adult and family Mass-journal users who follow the Sunday readings closely
notes: Form has a category dropdown — pick the general/other category, not "urgent". No published email address.

name: FOCUS (Fellowship of Catholic University Students)
fit: FOCUS runs student Bible studies as its central method — students with no money and patchy dorm wifi are close to the ideal user of a free offline Bible.
audienceDescription: College students and campus missionaries on 200+ US campuses; Bible studies are literally their core activity
notes: The email on both the contact and press pages is Cloudflare-obfuscated, so I did not capture it and did not try to decode it. Use the press room page as the route; a human opening it in a browser will see the address.

name: Franciscan Friars, Province of Saint Barbara — Communication Office
fit: A province with its own communication office and a bilingual outreach audience; Franciscan supporter newsletters reach a lot of daily-Scripture readers.
audienceDescription: Western US Franciscan province with a named Communication Office, a development office and a bilingual vocations office; publishes news and a supporter newsletter.
notes: Honest answer: this is the weakest entry here. The page lists a Communication Office but every email field renders blank — the addresses exist in the page markup but are not displayed, so there is no email a human visitor can read either. Phone (510) 536-3722, 1500 34th Avenue, Oakland CA. Phone is the only reliable public route. Include only if working the list by phone.

name: Franciscan Media
audienceSize: Not publicly stated in a form I could verify
fit: They already curate free daily Scripture and saint content for a broad lay audience and regularly point readers to free spiritual resources.
audienceDescription: Saint of the Day, daily reflections, Franciscan spirituality and prayer resources; long-established Cincinnati Catholic publisher with a broad devotional readership.
notes: Form only, with a department dropdown — choose 'General Contact', not 'Advertising/Sponsorships', since this is not a paid placement. Published address: 28 W. Liberty St., Cincinnati, OH 45202.

name: Franciscan Media / St. Anthony Messenger
fit: They run daily devotional email newsletters — a format where a one-line mention of a free offline Bible app reaches a lot of people who actually read Scripture daily.
audienceDescription: Publishing and digital ministry of the Franciscan Friars in Cincinnati; St. Anthony Messenger magazine, Saint of the Day, Minute Meditations and several long-running daily email newsletters with a large older-skewing subscriber base.
notes: No direct email or phone is published; the form has a department dropdown (General Contact, Customer Service, Technical Support, Donations, Advertising/Sponsorships). Choose General Contact — Advertising/Sponsorships would misrepresent this as a paid placement, which it is not. 28 W. Liberty St., Cincinnati.

name: Institute for Catholic Liberal Education
fit: They equip Catholic classroom teachers directly; a free offline Bible app suits schools with device restrictions and no budget.
audienceDescription: Catholic school teachers, principals, church leaders and parents renewing Catholic school education nationwide
notes: The site publishes an email but it is Cloudflare email-protected in the page source, so I am not reporting a decoded address. Use the contact form. Phone 844-425-3832 published.

name: Institute of Catholic Culture
fit: They give away structured adult catechesis for free on principle, and their students are doing real Scripture coursework. A free offline Bible is a natural companion resource for their course pages.
audienceDescription: Smaller but very serious adult-catechesis audience (roughly 20k on YouTube); free lecture courses in Scripture, patristics and Church history, with a large registered student list beyond YouTube.
notes: Their site is JavaScript-rendered and I could not read an email off the page, so I am not recording one. Search results suggest info@ and director@ addresses exist but I did not see them published — verify by opening the contact page in a browser before using anything other than the form.

name: Kolbe Academy
fit: Classical Catholic curriculum with heavy Scripture reading; they publish free tools and resources for families.
audienceDescription: Classical Catholic homeschool program and school, K-12, national enrollment
notes: I did not report an email here on purpose. The only address published on the contact page itself is techsupport@kolbe.org, which is the wrong inbox for this. A customerservice@kolbe.org address appears in their parent handbook contact list, but I could not load and confirm that page, so it is not included. Use the contact page / admissions appointment form.

name: Matt Fradd / Pints With Aquinas
fit: His audience is full of new and returning Catholics who ask basic practical questions like which Bible to use; a free one with no strings is easy for him to mention in passing.
audienceDescription: Very large long-form Catholic interview and apologetics audience, skewing young and male; heavy seeker and convert crossover.
notes: No usable public route found. pintswithaquinas.com now 301-redirects to his Daily Wire host page, and the only email I could find was a masked entry on a data-broker site, which I will not use or reconstruct. His YouTube About tab is behind the standard CAPTCHA, which I did not attempt. Realistically: either reach him via his Locals community, or deprioritise.

name: Minnesota Catholic Home Education Conference & Curriculum Fair
fit: Regional Catholic homeschool conferences hand out resource lists; a free app costs them nothing to include.
audienceDescription: Catholic homeschool families attending an annual regional conference and curriculum fair, plus a directory of Minnesota homeschool groups
notes: Two published addresses (general and vendor) were masked in what I could retrieve, so not reported — read them off the live contact page. Note that the vendor inbox is for paid exhibitors; this is not a vendor pitch, so use the general inbox and say plainly it is free and not for sale.

name: Mother of Divine Grace School (MODG)
fit: Well-known Catholic homeschool curriculum provider whose families do daily Scripture study.
audienceDescription: Large Catholic homeschool program (Ojai, CA) serving families nationally, K-12
notes: Contact form is the published route. A receptionist@modg.org address appears in third-party search results but I did not see it on their own page, so I have left the email blank rather than report an unverified one. Phone (805) 646-5818 published.

name: My Catholic Life! (Catholic Daily Reflections)
fit: They give away all their daily Scripture reflections free and explicitly build around daily Gospel reading — an exact philosophical and practical match for a free, no-ads Bible app.
audienceDescription: Daily Gospel meditation audience; very large free daily-email list alongside the channel, plus Divine Mercy and Passion-focused devotional content.
notes: Honest result: I could not find any published contact page or email. /contact-us/ and /about-us/ both 404 and the footer carries only the copyright line ('© 2026 My Catholic Life! Inc.'). Their YouTube About tab is the remaining route, which is CAPTCHA-gated — I did not attempt it. Worth a manual look for a contact link on catholic-daily-reflections.com before writing them off.

name: National Catholic Register
fit: One of the widest-reach US Catholic outlets; runs resource and Catholic-media coverage that regularly mentions apps.
audienceDescription: National Catholic newspaper (EWTN); large US Catholic readership, clergy and lay
notes: The contact page lists an editorial-services address but renders it behind Cloudflare email protection, so I am not recording an address I could not read directly. Open the contact page in a browser to reveal it. Phone (800) 356-9916.

name: Newman Catholic Student Center, University of Iowa
fit: A representative, unusually well-staffed campus Newman Center with a named Director of Outreach & Faith Formation — the person who picks what tools a student Bible study actually uses.
audienceDescription: Large, well-staffed Newman Center serving University of Iowa students, with dedicated directors of outreach and faith formation.
notes: Christine Wissink, Director of Outreach & Faith Formation, is the right person. Every staff email is published on the contact page but rendered behind anti-scraping obfuscation, so I am not reporting one; a human opening the page sees them. Center phone 319-337-3106. Treat this as a template — most Newman Centers publish staff emails the same way, so the segment scales by repeating this pattern campus by campus.

name: Newman Ministry / Newman Connection
fit: They distribute resources down to individual campus ministries, so one yes reaches many local student accounts.
audienceDescription: Catholic college students connected through 1,000+ campus ministries and Newman Centers
notes: Form only; no published email. Nonprofit — frame it as a resource for their campuses, not a product pitch.

name: Northwest Catholic (Archdiocese of Seattle)
fit: Runs features and practical resource pieces for a regional Catholic readership that includes many catechists and parish volunteers.
audienceDescription: Archdiocese of Seattle magazine and news site; Pacific Northwest Catholics, parish staff, catechists
notes: The contact page lists Kate DeWeese (Editor, 206-382-4870) and Jean Parietti (Features Editor, 206-382-4577), but their email addresses are obfuscated on the page, so I am not recording them. There is also a story-submission page at nwcatholic.org/submissions.

name: OSV News / Our Sunday Visitor
fit: OSV content feeds a large share of US diocesan papers and parish resource lists, so one mention travels far.
audienceDescription: National Catholic publisher and wire service supplying diocesan papers across the US
notes: The published contact page gives only phone numbers ((800) 348-2440, (260) 356-8400) and the Huntington, IN address - no editorial email. A newsroom address appears in search snippets but I could not confirm it on any OSV page, so it is not recorded. osvnews.com/contact and /contact-us both return 404.

name: Paulist Fathers — Office of Media Relations
fit: An order founded to use media for evangelization, with a standing media relations office. A free, no-ads, no-accounts Bible app is directly on-charism for them.
audienceDescription: US missionary society whose charism is literally media and evangelization — they run Busted Halo, Paulist Press and a SiriusXM radio show.
notes: Paul Snatchko, Director of Marketing and Communications; phone/text (412) 722-2907 is published in plain text. His email is on the page but obfuscated, so use the form or the phone. 415 West 59th St., New York.

name: Pray As You Go (Jesuits in Britain)
fit: Every daily session is built around a Scripture passage, and their audience is already in the habit of praying with Scripture on a phone. Offline access matters for the commuter use case they are built around.
audienceDescription: Daily Ignatian audio prayer with Scripture — very large UK/Ireland and international following, used heavily by commuters and by parish and school prayer groups.
notes: No published email — a form only. Run by Jesuits in Britain (registered charity CIO 1207742 / SC053495). The old pray-as-you-go.org domain now redirects to prayasyougo.org.

name: Pray More Novenas
fit: Their audience has already opted into a daily prayer reminder habit and would welcome a free companion Bible with no ads and no account to create.
audienceDescription: Very large novena-reminder email list plus retreat audience, run by John-Paul and Annie Deddens; devotional, habit-driven Catholic prayer audience.
notes: Honest result: their contact email appears throughout the Terms of Service but is masked by Cloudflare email obfuscation, so it is not actually published in readable form and I did not decode it. What is published in the clear: mailing address 55 Park Ave., Dayton, Ohio 45419, and the name John-Paul Deddens as their DMCA agent. There is no contact form. A human opening the page in a browser will see the address rendered.

name: Prayerful Rosary
fit: Mid-size, highly engaged daily-prayer audience; an independent creator is more likely than a large org to actually mention a free tool they genuinely like.
audienceDescription: Daily Rosary, chaplets, litanies and novenas; independent channel run by a creator who goes by Mikko.
notes: Honest result: the only site linked from the channel is a near-empty GitHub Pages page with no contact details. The About tab is CAPTCHA-gated and I did not attempt it. Note the channel also carries an unrelated crypto-hardware affiliate link, which is worth knowing before deciding to approach them.

name: Rosary Crew with Keith Nester (Down to Earth Ministry)
audienceSize: Not publicly stated in a form I could verify
fit: A convert-heavy audience that frequently arrives with a Protestant Bible and needs a Catholic one with the deuterocanon — and often cannot or will not pay for an app subscription.
audienceDescription: Daily live Rosary community led by Keith Nester, a former Protestant pastor; heavily convert-and-inquirer flavoured, very interactive.
notes: Form only; the form asks for parish/church, so fill that field honestly or leave it blank. Published: 48 Industrial Road, Elizabethtown, PA 17022; 717-367-0100. Keith Nester is Executive Director.

name: Studio Senn (Kortnee Senn)
fit: Her work is Scripture and saints illustration for families; her followers are exactly the people who'd want a clean, free Bible to read alongside it.
audienceDescription: Catholic families and art buyers following an illustrator and children's-book author (Seek and You Will Find, We Have a Pope)
notes: Form only on her own site. A gmail address for the studio circulates in search summaries, but it is not published on her contact page, so I have left it out — use the form.

name: The Catholic Crusade
fit: By far the biggest reach in this segment for pure pray-along content, and their viewers use a phone as their prayer book every single day.
audienceDescription: One of the largest Catholic prayer channels on YouTube — Rosaries, chaplets, litanies and novenas, pray-along format.
notes: Honest result: their only off-platform link is a Linktree, and it carries no website, contact form or email — just merchandise and affiliate links. The YouTube About tab is CAPTCHA-gated and I did not attempt it. A YouTube channel comment or the About tab opened manually by a person is the only realistic route.

name: The Catholic Homeschool
fit: Their contact form is literally built for submitting a 'group, resource, event, or organization' to be listed — the lowest-friction listing in this whole segment.
audienceDescription: Catholic homeschooling parents nationwide; directory of curricula, co-ops, support groups and state legal info
notes: The form asks for name of resource, website URL, state and description. No email published. Straightforward resource submission, no pitch needed.

name: The Catholic Talk Show
fit: They regularly do 'Catholic things you should know about' style segments; a free, no-catch Bible app is naturally mentionable content rather than an ad read.
audienceDescription: Mid-sized, broad general-Catholic audience; light, entertaining episodes on Catholic history, practice and curiosities. Strong podcast audience alongside YouTube.
notes: Form only — no email published. Note the domain is catholictalkshow.com (no leading 'the').

name: The Coming Home Network International
fit: Converts coming from Protestant backgrounds almost always ask which Catholic Bible to get and where the extra books are. A free offline Catholic edition answers that first question at zero cost.
audienceDescription: Converts and clergy converts to Catholicism, plus people actively discerning. Heavy Scripture-and-tradition content by nature of the convert journey.
notes: Their email is obfuscated behind Cloudflare email protection on the page, so it is not reliably readable without rendering — use the contact form. Phone (740) 450-1175 and a PO Box in Zanesville, OH are also published.

name: The Holy Rosary Channel
fit: Small enough that a personal note will actually be read, and the audience is squarely daily-prayer-on-a-phone.
audienceDescription: Small daily-Rosary pray-along channel with a consistent, committed core audience.
notes: Honest result: no external website or social links published on the channel page at all, and no business email visible outside the CAPTCHA-gated About tab, which I did not attempt. Lowest-priority entry in this list — included for completeness, not because the route is strong.

name: The Religion Teacher (Jared Dees)
fit: Audience is exactly catechists and Catholic religion teachers who regularly need free Scripture tools students can use on a phone without accounts.
audienceDescription: Catholic religion teachers and catechists; large email list and long-running resource blog for lesson planning
notes: No published email address — the contact form is the only route on the site. Verified the form fields directly (Name, Email, Subject, Message).
